transcript.text: fridge part freezin stuff, lettuce + yoghurts frozen solid at the back. hotpoint ff. any ideas pls

Common problem with Hotpoint fridge freezers. Work through these roughly in order, easiest first:

1. Check the temperature setting
• On a dial, the higher number is usually colder (e.g. 1 = warmest, 5 or 7 = coldest). People often turn it up thinking it's warmer. Aim for the middle (around 3).
• On a digital display, aim for 3–5°C in the fridge.
• Make sure Super Cool / Fast Freeze / Holiday mode hasn't been left on. Fast freeze on some models also chills the fridge harder.
• After changing anything, give it 24 hours to settle.

2. Keep food off the back wall
• Many Hotpoints have the cooling plate built into the fridge's back wall. Anything touching it (lettuce, yoghurts) will freeze, even if the temperature is set correctly.
• Leave a gap of 2–3 cm. If the back wall has a sheet of ice on it, that's partly normal (it should defrost and drip into the drain hole), but a thick build-up suggests a fault.

3. Don't block the air vents (frost-free models)
• If the freezer is frost-free, cold air is blown into the fridge through a vent, usually at the top back. Food right in front of it freezes, and blocking it can confuse the sensor.
• Keep the area clear, and don't pack the fridge too tightly.

4. Check where it's standing
• If it's in a garage, outbuilding or very cold room, many fridge freezers misbehave in the cold and can freeze the fridge side. Check the manual for its "climate class".
• Keep it away from heat sources too, like ovens and radiators.

5. Faulty part (if none of the above helps)
• Thermostat or temperature sensor (thermistor): if it's stuck, the fridge keeps cooling non-stop. You can test this by turning it to the warmest setting. If everything still freezes, this is the likely cause.
• Air damper/flap (frost-free models): it can stick open and let freezer air pour into the fridge.
• These parts are fairly cheap. Hotpoint's own engineer service or a local appliance repairer can fix them. Check if it's still under warranty (often 1 year, sometimes longer if you registered it).

Quick test: put a glass of water with a thermometer in the middle of the fridge overnight. If it reads well below 3°C on a middle setting, it's likely a faulty part rather than food placement.

If you tell me the model number (on a sticker inside the fridge) and whether the freezer is frost-free, I can be more specific.
dial is on max, kids prob moved it. fridge is rammed after big shop too, stuff against the vent at the back. model starts H8 but cant see the rest. no thermometer sorry

That's very likely the whole problem. Max setting plus food pressed against the vent will freeze things at the back.

What to do:
1. Turn the dial to the middle (about 3, or halfway). Hide it from the kids if you can, or show them it's not a toy!
2. Clear the back of the fridge. Move food forward so there's a few cm gap from the back wall and vent. If it's rammed, eat the fridge stuff down first or move drinks, condiments, or anything that will keep elsewhere.
3. Leave it 24 hours before judging. It takes a while to settle.
4. Bin or use up anything that's frozen and thawed badly (lettuce will go mushy; yoghurt is usually fine to eat but may go a bit grainy).

No thermometer? Quick check:
Put a glass of water in the middle of the fridge. After a few hours it should feel very cold but never have ice in it. If it's icy, nudge the dial one step warmer. A fridge thermometer is only a couple of quid from a supermarket or Amazon if you want to be sure (aim for 3-5°C).

Model number (in case you need it later):
Look for a sticker inside the fridge, usually on a side wall low down behind or beside the salad drawer. H8 models are usually frost-free, which fits the vent issue.

If it's still freezing after 24-48 hours on the middle setting with the back clear, that points to a fault (sensor or air flap), and that's when the model number will be handy for booking a repair.
